From cabd25b57216ddc132efbcc31f972baa03aad15a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@linaro.org>
Date: Tue, 9 Dec 2025 09:53:36 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] phy: stm32-usphyc: Fix off by one in probe()

The "index" variable is used as an index into the usbphyc->phys[] array
which has usbphyc->nphys elements.  So if it is equal to usbphyc->nphys
then it is one element out of bounds.  The "index" comes from the
device tree so it's data that we trust and it's unlikely to be wrong,
however it's obviously still worth fixing the bug.  Change the > to >=.

Fixes: 94c358da3a05 ("phy: stm32: add support for STM32 USB PHY Controller (USBPHYC)")
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@linaro.org>
Reviewed-by: Amelie Delaunay <amelie.delaunay@foss.st.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/aTfHcMJK1wFVnvEe@stanley.mountain
Signed-off-by: Vinod Koul <vkoul@kernel.org>

diff --git a/drivers/phy/st/phy-stm32-usbphyc.c b/drivers/phy/st/phy-stm32-usbphyc.c
index 27fe92f73f33..b44afbff8616 100644
--- a/drivers/phy/st/phy-stm32-usbphyc.c
+++ b/drivers/phy/st/phy-stm32-usbphyc.c
@@ -712,7 +712,7 @@ static int stm32_usbphyc_probe(struct platform_device *pdev)
 		}
 
 		ret = of_property_read_u32(child, "reg", &index);
-		if (ret || index > usbphyc->nphys) {
+		if (ret || index >= usbphyc->nphys) {
 			dev_err(&phy->dev, "invalid reg property: %d\n", ret);
 			if (!ret)
 				ret = -EINVAL;
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of the Patch

This patch fixes an off-by-one array bounds error in the STM32 USB PHY Controller driver.

### File Modified: `drivers/phy/st/phy-stm32-usbphyc.c`

- **Change:** In the `stm32_usbphyc_probe()` function, the condition `if (ret || index > usbphyc->nphys)` was changed to `if (ret || index >= usbphyc->nphys)`.
- **Explanation:** The variable `index` is used as an index into the `usbphyc->phys[]` array, which has `usbphyc->nphys` elements (valid indices are 0 to `nphys-1`). The original code allowed `index` to equal `nphys`, which would cause an out-of-bounds access. The fix ensures the check correctly rejects indices that are equal to or greater than the array size.

### Relationship between Modifications

The entire fix is contained within a single file. The change in the conditional expression directly addresses the root cause of the bug—a missing `=` in the bounds check. No other files or logic are affected.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
if (ret || index > usbphyc->nphys) {
Reason:
The condition uses `>` instead of `>=`. The array `usbphyc->phys[]` has `usbphyc->nphys` elements, whose valid indices range from 0 to `nphys - 1`. When `index` equals `nphys`, the condition is false, so the error handling is skipped. Subsequently using `index` to access `usbphyc->phys[port]` (which may later be used with `index`) or storing `index` in `usbphyc->phys[port]->index` leads to out-of-bounds access.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
if (ret || index >= usbphyc->nphys) {
Reason:
Changing `>` to `>=` ensures that when `index` equals `usbphyc->nphys`, the condition is true. The error is then correctly reported and the probe function returns an error, preventing any out-of-bounds access or use of an invalid index.
